newsitem.title: DENMARK: OECD sees '97 Danish GDP growth unchanged, '98 up.
newsitem.headline: OECD sees '97 Danish GDP growth unchanged, '98 up.

text.p: Denmark's economy is sound with low inflation, public budgets moving out of deficit and a stable currency, the Organisation for Economic Co-Operation and Development said on Tuesday.
The Paris-based OECD predicted Danish Gross Domestic Product (GDP) would grow by 2.5 percent this year, unchanged from the OECD's figure for 1996, and by 3.0 percent in 1998.
Danish government figures log a 2.4 percent GDP rise in 1996 and forecast a rise to 3.3 percent in 1997, falling back to 3.0 percent in 1998.
"Denmark continues to benefit from the now well-established strategy of fiscal consolidation, exchange-rate stability and labour market reform," the OECD said in its 1996/97 annual report.
"Employment growth and falling unemployment have coincided with low wage and price inflation, a current account surplus and public finances approaching balance," it added.
But it advised further efforts to cut unemployment, running at 7.9 percent in April, reverse a decline in the retirement age and make education more market-oriented.

It saw employment growing by one percent in 1997 and 1998 and inflation staying below 2.75 percent. Calculated by European Union methods Denmark's consumer price index (CPI) rose by 2.1 percent in 1996.
But the report said the inflation outlook could be upset by rising property prices and the danger of a labour shortage pushing up wages.

"With signs of excess demand for labour already appearing in several regions and occupations and with house prices rising, the eventual risk of deteriorating wage competitiveness...and of an inflationary consumption-led boom cannot be fully discounted," it said.
It saw the current account surplus stable at around one percent of GDP and said that the future looked bright if current conditions were maintained.
"The prospects for continued expansion are good, based on the credibility of the monetary policy framework and the prospects of further budget consolidation," the report said.
